name: Leaf Tessellation
description: Sunlight capture optimization through tessellated leaf arrangement. Venation networks act as flow systems distributing water and sugars. Phyllotaxis follows golden-angle spirals to minimize self-shading, embodying phi-driven packing efficiency.

core_attributes.pattern: sunlight capture optimization, venation flow networks, phyllotaxis

scope.definition: Fraction of incident sunlight intercepted by leaf canopy using phyllotaxis-optimized arrangement versus random leaf placement at equivalent leaf area index (LAI=3), measured in 3D light simulation models.

evidence.source: Honda & Fisher (1978) 'Tree branch angle: maximizing effective leaf area', Science 199:888-890; Valladares & Niinemets (2008) 'Shade tolerance, a key plant feature of complex nature', Annual Review of Ecology Evolution.
cross_domain_examples: Fibonacci phyllotaxis in sunflower: adjacent leaf angles at 137.5° (golden angle) minimizes self-shading — 0.94 light interception
spiral leaf arrangement: reduces overlap to near-zero for vertical sun angles — geometric optimization
rice paddy architecture: erect leaf angle selected to maximize canopy light interception for yield

scope.falsifiability: If random leaf placement achieves statistically equivalent light interception to phyllotaxis-arranged equivalents at LAI=3, spiral arrangement provides no light-capture advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Efficiency depends on sun elevation angle and leaf angle distribution. Phyllotaxis advantage is greatest at low sun elevations common in temperate latitudes. Leaf reflectance and transmission affect canopy absorption.
